No monopoly, can't build; don't mortgage. Must keep ~$160 for bank Virginia to finish pink (St Charles+States), then houses, plus cushion vs p3 brown hotels ($450). Don't sell either orange (hands p2 the best set) or Vermont (cheap light-blue monopoly p4 can house now). Don't bid for NY — premium plus houses leaves me unable to survive another Baltic hit. End; buy Virginia on sight."}}
message.reasoning:
I need to make a decision in this Monopoly turn.

I have $897 and six properties. I need Virginia Avenue to complete the pink set. I am two-thirds of the way through the orange set. Player 2 has $1153 and owns Reading Railroad, New York Avenue, Indiana, and Marvin Gardens.

Player 3 has $706 and owns hotels on Mediterranean and Baltic, plus Electric Company and Boardwalk. Player 4 has $614 and owns Oriental, Connecticut, Pennsylvania RR, Kentucky, Ventnor, Pennsylvania Ave, Short Line, and Park Place. Virginia Avenue is unowned. I will not sell orange to player 2 or Vermont to player 4.

I cannot buy property during post-turn actions. I am considering trading New York Avenue from player 2 to complete the orange set.

Player 2 values the orange set highly and previously offered $450 for both properties. I would likely need to pay $400–$500 for New York Avenue. That leaves me with only about $400, which is too little to build houses or survive player 3’s brown hotels.

Player 2 will not sell New York Avenue cheaply. Player 4 owns Oriental and Connecticut, which would complete a light blue monopoly for a much lower price than the orange set.

I will end my turn and stay liquid. I will buy Virginia Avenue when I land there. I will not trade for monopolies.

I considered trading with player 4 for Park Place or Boardwalk, but dark blue monopolies are too expensive to build. I also checked the remaining unowned properties: Illinois is still bank-owned, and the red, yellow, and green sets are split between the other players.
